key_insight: IRMAE-WD’s latent singular-value drop identifies the trained representation’s effective dimension, not an intrinsic turbulence dimension; coordinate counts should be tied to target accuracy or scale.
engineering_relevance: IRMAE-WD can compress minimal-channel velocity fields more efficiently than POD up to about 97% reconstruction, supporting compact representations for flow modeling.
method: Apply a 3D convolutional IRMAE-WD autoencoder to minimal-channel velocity fields at Reτ = 110.
Vary the number of linear layers and truncate latent coordinates at the singular-value drop.
Use transfer learning to compare coordinate requirements against POD by reconstruction accuracy and reproduced scale.
evidence_signal: Truncation at the drop reduced reconstruction rate by at most 0.01 percentage points; IRMAE-WD reproduced a given scale with fewer coordinates than POD, but POD needed fewer above about 97% reconstruction.
watch_item: The drop shifts toward fewer dimensions as linear layers are added, so it should not be treated as a universal physical degree-of-freedom count.
paper_title: Effective-dimension estimation of a minimal turbulent channel flow via IRMAE-WD
